data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) defines the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) requirements for the management and use of secure communication devices, material, and systems that protect Classified National Security Information (CNSI) to ensure that:
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) requirements for the management and use of secure communication devices, material, and systems that protect Classified National Security Information (CNSI)

policy_statements.source_text: Secure communication assets are appropriately managed and controlled;
The area(s) where equipment is stored or used is approved and accredited by the Office of Homeland Security’s (OHS) Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD) or CNSI Staff (CNSIS);
policy_statements.target: area(s) where equipment is stored or used

policy_statements.source_text: CNSI users are properly trained and made aware of their responsibilities by members of the OHS’ National Security Systems Program (NSSP) and OHS/PDSD/CNSIS; and
The activities of the user community, OHS PDSD, and NSSP are coordinated.
policy_statements.target: activities of the user community, OHS PDSD, and NSSP

policy_statements.source_text: This policy complies with Executive Order (EO) 13526, Classified National Security Information; Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) directives, policies, and instructions; National Security Agency (NSA) security doctrines; Intelligence Community Directives (ICD) issued by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI); and USDA directives, which establish, implement, and support secure communications for the protection of CNSI.
cross_references: Executive Order (EO) 13526, Classified National Security Information

policy_statements.source_text: Guidance references are provided in Appendix C, Authorities and References of this document.
policy_statements.target: Appendix C, Authorities and References of this document

policy_statements.source_text: This policy supersedes DR 3300-015, Secure Communications Systems, dated July 14, 2016, in its entirety.
cross_references: DR 3300-015, Secure Communications Systems, dated July 14, 2016

policy_statements.source_text: This policy will remain in effect until superseded or expiration.
conditions: until superseded or expiration

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of its publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of its publication date

policy_statements.source_text: CNSI is also referred to as classified information.
Confidential business information and proprietary information are not the same as classified information.
policy_statements.target: Confidential business information and proprietary information

policy_statements.source_text: This policy applies to all USDA secure communications systems (e.g., telephones, mobile telephones, video teleconference systems, servers, laptop and desktop computers, applications, and wireless devices) that are developed, maintained, or operated by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, political appointees, contractors, or other individuals working for or on behalf of the USDA.
policy_statements.target: all USDA secure communications systems (e.g., telephones, mobile telephones, video teleconference systems, servers, laptop and desktop computers, applications, and wireless devices)
conditions: that are developed, maintained, or operated by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, political appointees, contractors, or other individuals working for or on behalf of the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This policy only applies to classified systems and national security systems used for the transmission and processing of CNSI.
policy_statements.target: classified systems and national security systems used for the transmission and processing of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental Manual (DM) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual, provides guidance for the protection of CNSI.
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS NSSP will be the primary office in the USDA to acquire and manage all telecommunication, computer, and network systems used to process, transmit, and store CNSI.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that need access to secure communication systems will request support through the USDA NSSP Manager (NSSPM).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that need access to secure communication systems

policy_statements.source_text: Electronic transmission of classified information will be made via secure telephone, secure radio system, secure video teleconferencing system, secure data network, or a secure facsimile device, protected by an NSA-approved controlled cryptographic item (CCI), encryption device, or other NSA-approved architecture.
Only devices validated by NSA and approved by the USDA for the transmission of CNSI will be used in USDA.
policy_statements.target: devices validated by NSA and approved by the USDA for the transmission of CNSI
conditions: validated by NSA and approved by the USDA for the transmission of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: A list of approved secure communication devices can be obtained by contacting the NSSP Office.
policy_statements.target: list of approved secure communication devices

policy_statements.source_text: Only authorized personnel may use, install, remove, or relocate any secure, non-mobile communication device without prior approval from the USDA Communications Security (COMSEC) Manager.
conditions: without prior approval from the USDA Communications Security (COMSEC) Manager

policy_statements.source_text: Only authorized personnel may use mobile devices for the processing or transmission of CNSI.
conditions: for the processing or transmission of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Users will adhere to the applicable NSA Security Doctrine for mobile devices.
policy_statements.target: applicable NSA Security Doctrine for mobile devices
cross_references: NSA Security Doctrine for mobile devices

policy_statements.source_text: COMSEC devices (e.g., terminals or cryptographic material) may only be issued to specific approved individuals.
policy_statements.target: COMSEC devices (e.g., terminals or cryptographic material)
conditions: specific approved individuals

policy_statements.source_text: These devices cannot be re-issued to another individual without first being returned to the USDA COMSEC Manager for proper inventory management.
conditions: without first being returned to the USDA COMSEC Manager for proper inventory management

policy_statements.source_text: Secure Equipment and Systems Requests to Process CNSI
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices requesting CNSI systems will adhere to USDA and Federal policies and regulations for secure equipment.
policy_statements.target: USDA and Federal policies and regulations for secure equipment
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: requesting CNSI systems

policy_statements.source_text: Security guidelines and requirements outlined in DM 3440-001 and DM 3300-015, Secure Communication Systems will be met to ensure the security of CNSI.
policy_statements.target: Security guidelines and requirements outlined in DM 3440-001 and DM 3300-015, Secure Communication Systems

policy_statements.source_text: The requesting Mission Area, agency, or staff office will incur the costs associated with the acquisition of the requested system and the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) funding requirements for it.
policy_statements.target: costs associated with the acquisition of the requested system and the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) funding requirements for it
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will identify their requirements for a CNSI system on form Agriculture Department (AD)-3084, Justification for a Classified National Security Information System, and submit it to the USDA OHS NSSP office, per DM 3300-015.
policy_statements.target: their requirements for a CNSI system
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: Agriculture Department (AD)-3084, Justification for a Classified National Security Information System

policy_statements.source_text: System requests will be reviewed and signed by a Mission Area, agency, or staff office approving authority before the documentation is submitted to the USDA OHS NSSP office.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office approving authority
conditions: before the documentation is submitted to the USDA OHS NSSP office

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of OHS will:
Ensure secure communication technical assistance is available to Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices;
Serve as the Designated Approving Authority (DAA) for information and telecommunication systems used to process CNSI.
policy_statements.target: information and telecommunication systems used to process CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: The DAA will:
Review and approve, or disapprove, all CNSI system requests; and
Ensure that all applicable assessment and authorization (A&A) processes required for the implementation of the identified technical solution are properly addressed;
policy_statements.target: all applicable assessment and authorization (A&A) processes required for the implementation of the identified technical solution

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee the USDA OHS NSSP office;

Designate an NSSPM with oversight responsibility for the development, implementation, and evaluation of the USDA classified information systems A&A program, per the Committee on National Security Systems Policy (CNSSP) 22, Cybersecurity Risk Management Policy, dated August 31, 2016;
cross_references: Committee on National Security Systems Policy (CNSSP) 22, Cybersecurity Risk Management Policy, dated August 31, 2016

policy_statements.source_text: Provide sufficient resources to support the USDA NSSP;
Provide guidance, direction, and oversight for the security of processes and secure communication systems;
policy_statements.target: security of processes and secure communication systems

policy_statements.source_text: Provide direction, oversight, and concurrence review functions for the USDA A&A process for secure communication systems;
policy_statements.target: USDA A&A process for secure communication systems

policy_statements.source_text: Review agency and staff office policy exception requests and render decisions per Section 7, Policy Exceptions, of this DR;
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office policy exception requests

policy_statements.source_text: Approve or disapprove all requirements and requests for systems used to process CNSI after review of the information provided by PDSD and USDA NSSP; and
policy_statements.target: all requirements and requests for systems used to process CNSI
conditions: after review of the information provided by PDSD and USDA NSSP

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an oversight role to ensure consistent and effective implementation of secure communication systems.
Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners will:
Coordinate all CNSI telecommunications requirements with the USDA NSSPM;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners

policy_statements.source_text: Identify and provide initial acquisition funding and O&M funding, as appropriate, to support the requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
policy_statements.target: initial acquisition funding and O&M funding
conditions: as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Identify a Federal or contractor point of contact (POC), who is knowledgeable in all aspects of the request and can assist the reviewing entities with questions during the request process and review of the documents.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
policy_statements.target: Federal or contractor point of contact (POC)
conditions: who is knowledgeable in all aspects of the request and can assist the reviewing entities with questions during the request process and review of the documents

policy_statements.source_text: The POC will adhere to USDA and Federal policies and regulations regarding the use of the system requested;
policy_statements.target: USDA and Federal policies and regulations regarding the use of the system requested

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the USDA NSSPM all support agreements for managed CNSI services from non-USDA entities;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
policy_statements.target: all support agreements for managed CNSI services from non-USDA entities

policy_statements.source_text: Register CNSI systems with the USDA NSSP office in accordance with DM 3300-015, and provide required resources to complete A&A for the respective classified stand-alone computer systems;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners

policy_statements.source_text: Consult with the USDA NSSPM to initiate the necessary procurement actions to obtain CCI and system components used for the processing or transmission of CNSI;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
policy_statements.target: necessary procurement actions to obtain CCI and system components used for the processing or transmission of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the protection of CCI, and notify the USDA COMSEC manager within 12 hours of the discovery of the loss of COMSEC keys or equipment used to process or transmit CNSI;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
conditions: within 12 hours of the discovery of the loss of COMSEC keys or equipment used to process or transmit CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Notify the USDA NSSPM and PDSD a minimum of 30 calendar days prior to the relocation of any secure communication equipment, to provide ample time to coordinate logistical changes or address security concerns with the OHS PDSD Classified National Security Information Staff;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
conditions: a minimum of 30 calendar days prior to the relocation of any secure communication equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Upon request, assist the COMSEC manager with semiannual inventory and equipment maintenance tasks; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners
conditions: Upon request

policy_statements.source_text: Contact the USDA COMSEC manager prior to transfer, reassignment, or any absence of the hand receipt holder exceeding 30 calendar days, to allow for a secure transfer of equipment and delegation of responsibility prior to the receipt holder’s departure.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency and staff office system owners

Verify the security clearance of all personnel who manage, operate, configure, and certify telecommunication and computer systems used to process CNSI;

policy_statements.source_text: Certify that the identified location has been approved for processing of CNSI;
Coordinate CNSI information technology matters with the USDA NSSPM;
Respond to employee questions on protecting classified information or working in a space approved for the processing and discussion of CNSI;
